title: Shadowmoon Valley
body: Shadowmoon Valley lies in the far southeast of Outland, a land of ash, black rock and rivers of green fel lava under a dim and smoky sky. The orcs of the Shadowmoon clan once honored their ancestors here, and at its eastern edge the draenei raised the Temple of Karabor, one of their holiest sites. Both were lost to the Horde. Gul'dan's warriors took Karabor and the Shadow Council made it their seat, and the warlock raised the volcano at the valley's center in a ritual that severed the orcs from the elements of Draenor. The temple, now called the Black Temple, became the throne of Illidan Stormrage, and his servants, fel orcs and naga, Broken and blood elves, hold the valley in his name. The Burning Legion bombards it from Legion Hold. Against them stand the Wildhammer dwarves, the Horde's Kor'kron, and the Aldor and Scryers of Shattrath, while the Netherwing drakes struggle against the Dragonmaw orcs who enslave them.

title: Wildhammer Stronghold
body: Wildhammer Stronghold stands in the southwest of the valley, the fortress of Kurdran Wildhammer, thane of the Wildhammer in Outland, and his gryphon riders. It is a hard place to hold. Infernals fall on its walls from Legion Hold to the northwest, Illidan's minions press from the other side, and Wing Commander Nuainn's riders have fought so long without relief that they are ragged with exhaustion. The ground itself is restless: the stronghold was built over the ancestral grounds of the Shadowmoon orcs, and the spirits of the old clan, dormant for nearly twenty years, now wander its courtyards. Zorus the Judicator studies them, while the gnome Gnomus, an inventor turned gourmand, dreams only of food that never cools.

title: Shadowmoon Village
body: Shadowmoon Village is the Horde's outpost in the northwest of the valley, held by Overlord Or'barokh and the elite Kor'kron guard. Like the dwarves to the south it lives under the Legion's guns: infernals from Legion Hold to the southwest rain on its walls, and Blood Guard Gulmok drafts every able fighter onto the line. The village is haunted as well. Chief Apothecary Hildagard warns that the land is full of ghosts, and she can craft goggles that reveal the spirits of Shadowmoon zealots drifting among the buildings. Nearby, the blood elf Researcher Tiorus studies the heat-proof diemetradons of the lava flows with probes built by his former partner, the gnome Gnomus, who resents it.

title: Legion Hold
body: Legion Hold is the Burning Legion's fortress in western Shadowmoon, the source of the infernals that pound both the Wildhammer and the Horde outposts, for the Legion stocks and prepares its infernals there. Terrormasters and Shadow Council warlocks guard the stockpile, and the pit lords Makazradon and Morgroron stalk its grounds. Beside the hold, the Fetid Pool festers around the wreckage of a fallen fel reaver. High in the northern mountains lies Invasion Point: Cataclysm, where fel reaver sentinels stand guard over still more infernals.

parts.body: Spies who crept into the hold in disguise and listened at its communication device learned who directs this war. An image of Warbringer Razuun, speaking in the name of Doom Lord Kazzak, ordered the hold's commander to step up the attacks and destroy the orcish and dwarven strongholds with all haste, and promised all the infernals he needed from the Deathforge.

parts.body: Razuun's own orders, taken when he fell at the Deathforge, gave away the Legion's true staging ground. The great store of infernals waits at Invasion Point: Cataclysm, and the only way to reach it is a teleporter inside Legion Hold, worked by control devices that certain of the hold's demons carry.

title: The Deathforge
body: The Deathforge is a Shadow Council foundry dug into the rock between the two outposts, where infernals are made as fast as the Legion can hurl them. Mo'arg smiths and tinkerers work the forges, and the scouts reckon that somewhere below ground the warlocks keep a summoning chamber, calling up the corrupted elementals that become the hearts of the infernals. Two scouting parties watch from the heights, the dwarves of Deathforge Tower and the orcs of Slag Watch, under strict orders to observe and not to fight. Each sent one of its own inside, the Wildhammer Flanis Swiftwing, who volunteered to spy, and the orc Kagrosh, who wanted to be a hero, and neither has been heard from since.

parts.body: Flanis never came out. He was discovered and slain in the midst of his spy mission, and the forge's attendants left his corpse in the open, perhaps as a warning to other interlopers. Stormer Ewan Wildwing doubts that Flanis ever understood how heavily the forge was guarded until it was too late.

title: Illidari Point
body: Illidari Point lies in the southwest, between Legion Hold and Wildhammer Stronghold. It is the proving ground for Illidan's demons, those who abandoned the Burning Legion to serve the Betrayer, and satyrs, shadowstalkers and succubi gather there under his lieutenant Lothros. Succubi led by Painmistress Gabrissa work their rituals around a rune ringed by hovering demonic crystals, and the beams that pour from those crystals hold the body of an orc suspended in the air above it.

parts.body: The dead orc is Ar'tor, the youngest son of Oronok Torn-heart, a gifted hunter and tracker who came here hunting a piece of the Cipher of Damnation. No one can say how long he has been dead. The demonic magic that holds his body in the air takes from him even in death.

title: Sketh'lon and the Magma Fields
body: The Sketh'lon arakkoa once camped in western Shadowmoon, and their ruins remain: the Sketh'lon Wreckage northwest of the Deathforge, and the Sketh'lon Base Camp to the south, east of Wildhammer Stronghold. Their ghosts linger as the Dark Conclave, wielding powers no one knew they possessed, and they prey on the orc peons sent to cut wood among the ruins, draining their lives to feed their magic. The peons are sure the place is cursed. Between the two outposts the road crosses the Magma Fields, where lava flows through cracks in the ground and felfire diemetradons bask in the heat.

parts.body: The arakkoa died in the days when the Horde massed under Gul'dan. Seeing the threat, they planned to strike at him first, but Gul'dan learned of their intentions and answered with a mighty spell that destroyed their camps and twisted the spirits of those who dwelt there.

title: The Hand of Gul'dan
body: The Hand of Gul'dan is the great volcano at the center of the valley, raised by the warlock Gul'dan in the ritual that tore the orcs away from the elements. Fel lava still pours down its sides, and its lava long ago buried the draenei village of Baa'ri. On its flanks the Fel Pits seethe with enraged spirits of fire and earth, and the Ashtongue Corruptors Eykenen and Uylaru, once shaman who now defile the elements they revered, tend corrupt totems among them. The Scalding Pools lie near the summit. Spectral riders, the Ghostriders of Karabor, circle the mountain on the roads around its base, and the fel beast Uvuros, wanted dead by both outposts, prowls its slopes.

title: The Altar of Damnation
body: On the western outskirts of the Hand of Gul'dan stands the Altar of Damnation, where Gul'dan spoke the words that shattered this land. The moment has left its mark. A memory of the warlock still stands at the altar among the kneeling spirits of the damned, and beside him linger remnants of his hate, greed, malice, pride and corruption. Earthmender Torlok and Earthmender Gorboto of the Earthen Ring keep watch there, seeking to commune with the tortured elements. Gul'dan was not content to destroy the draenei, Torlok says: he razed Draenor itself and siphoned off its energies for his war, and all that is left here are the remnants of his madness.

title: Coilskar Point
body: Coilskar Point and the cistern to its east are the lair of the Coilskar naga, servants of Illidan, who have seized the only clean water left in Shadowmoon Valley. They foul it for their own ends, and the agitated pools around their villages howl with the anguish of enraged water spirits. The earthmender Wilda came seeking the source of the spirits' distress and was taken prisoner, held in a watery cell beside other captive spirits. Lady Shav'rar commands at the point, and Coilskar sorceresses guard the cistern.

parts.body: The naga hide more than water. Grom'tor, eldest son of Oronok Torn-heart, beat the truth out of a Coilskar commander after five others had told him nothing: a fragment of the Cipher of Damnation lies in one of the naga chests at Coilskar Point or the cistern, and the naga carry the keys.

title: Oronok's Farm
body: High on the Shattered Shelf above Coilskar Cistern, a weathered orc keeps a campfire and a herd of trained felboars. He calls himself Oronok Torn-heart, hermit and farmer, and his boars root tubers out of the hard earth of the Shattered Plains below. The plains are not kind to farmers: ravenous flayers from a nest to the northeast prey on his animals, and a flayer matriarch guards their eggs. Oronok invites travelers to warm themselves by his fire and warns them of the beasts of the shelf.

parts.body: The farmer's life is a masquerade, a test for those who come asking questions, and Oronok is no more a farmer than they are. Long ago he stood at Gul'dan's side as one of the warlock's lieutenants, and he was at the Altar of Damnation on the day the land was shattered.

title: Ruins of Baa'ri
body: Baa'ri was a draenei village, rich in relics of religious importance, until the Hand of Gul'dan rose and buried it under lava with its people. Now Illidan has set the Ashtongue Broken to dig it out. Scores of Ashtongue workers labor in the ruins under Illidari overseers and Akama's lieutenant, Oronu the Elder, who receives written orders from his master daily, and handlers drive elekk demolishers through the rubble. Among the treasures buried here are the Tablets of Baa'ri, said to hold the secrets of the Temple of Karabor, and the Aldor and the Scryers both send agents to reach them first.

parts.body: The tablets told of another treasure kept at Baa'ri: a Medallion of Karabor. Only the highest-ranking draenei priests were granted such medallions, for they opened the way into the Temple of Karabor, and both orders want to know whether the Ashtongue have dug it up yet.

title: The Warden's Cage
body: South of the Ruins of Baa'ri, the Warden's Cage is a prison held by Akama and his Ashtongue Deathsworn, said to be the vilest and most brutal of the tribe. Among their enemies it is whispered to be a torture chamber, and the Aldor and the Scryers alike call Akama both evil and cunning. His second in command here is a Broken named Sanoru. Above the prison walls a satyr named Zandras keeps watch over everything that happens below.

parts.body: The satyr is Illidan's spy, and the Deathsworn suffer him only until they can be rid of him. Those who prove they are not with Illidan are shown what he cannot see: beyond the halls, an underground passage hidden by stagnant water leads to a secret chamber, Akama's hideout, and none who enter may speak of it.

title: Altar of Sha'tar
body: The Altar of Sha'tar is the Aldor's outpost in Shadowmoon, standing northwest of the Black Temple. From here the draenei priesthood carries its war against Illidan and the Legion to their very doorstep. Exarch Onaala, who trained as an anchorite in days when female exarchs were all but unheard of, leads the outpost, holding that courage and conviction count for more than anything else. Anchorite Ceyla studies the secrets of Karabor, Vindicator Aluumen sends fighters against the Ashtongue at Baa'ri and the fel orcs on the holy Ata'mal Terrace, and Harbinger Saronen gathers the insignias of the Legion's officers.

parts.body: The Dragonmaw would gladly see the altar burned, for it stands across their lines to Coilskar, and Overlord Mor'ghor has ordered a battalion of his Skybreakers to sack it. The order reached Anchorite Ceyla by way of the very commander sent to carry it out, and the Aldor mean to turn the attack to their own advantage.

title: Ruins of Karabor
body: The Ruins of Karabor lie before the walls of the Black Temple, and Illidan has turned them into a training ground for demon hunters. Sunfury blood elves, soldiers of Prince Kael'thas, arrive in numbers to learn the art, dressing and fighting like Illidan himself, while Sunfury warlocks summon and bind demons for the initiates to battle. The grounds are run by the blood elf Varedis, with three night elf demon hunters, Alandien, Theras and Netharel, at his side. One prisoner is too dangerous even for these lessons: the pit lord Azaloth, held banished in the ruins and seething at his captors.

parts.body: Varedis is no ordinary pupil. He was one of five warriors Kael'thas sent to train under Illidan, the first blood elves ever allowed to become demon hunters. Three died in the trials and one went mad; Varedis alone survived, and within a year he surpassed the three masters set to teach him. Then he stole into the Shadow Council and committed to memory the Book of Fel Names, said to hold the true name of every demon.

parts.body: The training grounds have lost their masters. Agents of the Aldor and the Scryers burned the Book of Fel Names before Varedis as he took his demon form, stripping him of his power, and he fell at Karabor with Alandien, Theras and Netharel.

title: Ata'mal Terrace
body: The Ata'mal Terrace beside the Black Temple was once one of the draenei's holiest sites, where ata'mal crystals were used in their spiritual ceremonies. Now the fel orcs of the Shadowmoon clan, Illidan's most feared army, hold it. Slayers, chosen and darkweavers crowd its tiers alongside shadowsworn drakonid, and Shadowlord Deathwail circles high above the terrace, out of reach. The Aldor once had reason to believe an ata'mal crystal was hidden somewhere nearby, but their scrying has revealed nothing.

parts.body: The scrying failed for a reason. The fel orcs guard an ata'mal crystal called the Heart of Fury at the top of the terrace, clouded in dark magic to hide it from the Sha'tar, and it can be reached only once Deathwail and his warlocks are slain. Deathwail swears that its power belongs to Illidan.

Since the Shattered Sun Offensive took up its war on the Isle of Quel'Danas, its smiths have wanted those armaments for their forges.

title: The Black Temple
body: The Black Temple was once the Temple of Karabor, the great sanctuary of the draenei. Gul'dan's Horde took it, the Shadow Council made it their seat, and the warlock kept his private quarters inside. Later the pit lord Magtheridon ruled from it, until Illidan Stormrage drove him out with the help of Akama's Broken and claimed the temple as his throne. The ghosts of the clerics of Karabor, murdered by Teron Gorefiend after the city fell, still roam before its walls. Now the naaru Xi'ri gathers Aldor and Scryer soldiers on the approach to the temple, and before its walls stalks Doomwalker, the fel reaver Kil'jaeden sent against its gates, said to be infused with the souls of martyred draenei.

parts.body: In time the temple no longer shielded its master. Champions from Shattrath fought their way through its halls to the summit, and Illidan Stormrage was struck down in the seat he had taken from Magtheridon. Word spread across Outland that the Betrayer was dead.

title: Netherwing Fields
body: East of the Hand of Gul'dan, fields of enormous blue crystals jut from the earth, and nether drakes wheel above them. These are the Netherwing, a young flight born of black dragon eggs that were steeped in raw nether energy. They are frightened now, too afraid of the Dragonmaw to come down even to feed, and some fall dead from exhaustion; Mordenai, who keeps watch over the fields, does what he can to save them. Rocknail flayers, the drakes' natural prey, swarm among the crystals. Past the fields, Netherwing Pass leads on to the Altar of Shadows, a lonely shrine where the spirit of an ancient Shadowmoon orc is said to reside.

parts.body: The ancient spirit is no harmless ghost. It is Teron Gorefiend, and the Altar of Shadows is his prison, kept by Karsius the Ancient Watcher. With his armor, cloak and truncheon restored, Gorefiend needs only a living body to carry him past his jailers and break his bonds.

title: Sanctum of the Stars
body: The Sanctum of the Stars is the Scryers' outpost in Shadowmoon, standing at the foot of the Netherwing Fields. For these blood elves the war runs on two fronts: against Illidan, and against the Sunfury of Prince Kael'thas, whose ranks keep swelling with pilgrims from Quel'Thalas. Battlemage Vyara warns that the Scryers must outrecruit Kael or, once recruits run short, outkill him. Arcanist Thelis and Larissa Sunstrike pursue Illidan's secrets, and Varen the Reclaimer leads strikes on the Ashtongue and on the Ata'mal fel orcs, who once fell on the sanctum in a savage attack.

parts.body: The Dragonmaw covet the site, for it cuts their lines to Eclipse Point and Illidari Point, and Overlord Mor'ghor has ordered a battalion of his Skybreakers to sack it. The order reached Arcanist Thelis by way of the very commander sent to carry it out, and the Scryers mean to turn the attack to their own advantage.

title: Eclipse Point
body: Eclipse Point is a terraced ruin in the south of the valley, held by the Eclipsion, blood elves in Illidan's service under Grand Commander Ruusk, and a bridge to its north looks out over the road up to it. The elves guard their charges closely. The Rod of Lianthe lies locked in a strongbox in a pavilion on the top tier, heavily guarded, and their dragonhawks see through disguises that fool the elves themselves. The Scryers prize the Sunfury signets worn by its high-ranking officers, allies of both Kael'thas and Illidan.

parts.body: From the shadows of the bridge, Borak, son of Oronok, has watched the elves for weeks. They hide a third of the Cipher of Damnation, and all he has learned is that Illidan sends an envoy from the Black Temple once a day, an envoy whose bodyguard never leaves his side.

title: The Path of Conquest
body: The Path of Conquest lies just east of Eclipse Point, and there Illidan's Eclipsion armies muster soldiers, cavaliers and spellbinders for a great advance. At its southern end, by a stationary caravan, Chancellor Bloodleaf seeks to win Corok the Mighty and the giants of Shadowmoon to Illidan's side, reminding them that Illidan's enemies are destroyed. To the west the crazed colossi of the Eclipsion Fields wander. Also at the path's southern end stands Crimson Watch, held by soldiers of the Crimson Sigil, where Marcus Auralion, High General of the Sha'tar, floats inside a crystal prison.

parts.body: The courtship of the giants failed. Struck by attackers who looked like Illidan's own elves, the crazed colossi proved to be the children of Behemothon, King of the Colossi, who swore that the pact was broken and that giant would never side with elf.

parts.body: A journal taken from Val'zareq the Conqueror, who paraded along the path, told how he captured the high general himself. Auralion knows his jailers: the Crimson Sigil are Illidan's elite, at the top of the chain of command for every Illidari force outside the Black Temple, speaking directly with the Betrayer and carrying out his orders without question.

title: Dragonmaw Fortress
body: Dragonmaw Fortress rises on the eastern edge of the Netherwing Fields, the stronghold of the Dragonmaw orcs who serve Illidan. Here the clan does to the nether drakes what it once did to the red dragons of Azeroth: wranglers and subjugators capture them and torture them until they bend, and many broken drakes now carry Dragonmaw drake-riders into battle. Atop the fortress, bound in chains, Karynaku, mate of Neltharaku and mother of the flight, is held prisoner. Her jailer is the clan's chieftain, the ancient orc Zuluhed the Whacked.

parts.body: Karynaku is free. Her chains sapped her strength, and Zuluhed hid in her thoughts waiting for her to break, so she called him to her with a false promise to obey. When the old chieftain came, he was slain for the key to her bonds.

title: Netherwing Ledge
body: Netherwing Ledge was once part of the Shadowmoon mainland; now it floats in the sky off the valley's broken southeastern shelf. It was the Netherwing's sanctuary until the Dragonmaw took it. At Dragonmaw Base Camp, Overlord Mor'ghor drives peons and Murkblood Broken to strip the island of its crystals, ore and netherdust pollen to supply Illidan's armies, and transporters carry the haul to the fortress along the Dragonmaw Skyway. Above the ledge the drake Vhel'kur, spawn of Deathwing, flies an endless circle around the island that was his home and is now his grave, still seething at his defeat by Teron Gorefiend.

title: Netherwing Mines
body: The Netherwing Mines bore deep into Netherwing Ledge, where the Dragonmaw set Murkblood Broken to dig. The work stopped when a miner's pick struck a crystal formation that turned out to be part of a sleeping nether dragon, Toranaku. The dragon woke in fury and slaughtered the workers, the creatures of the depths rose with it, and a band of miners cut off from the exit soon sank into madness. The Dragonmaw call it a grim discovery, and the surviving miners would rather die than dig any deeper.

parts.body: It was no accident. The Netherwing offered the Murkblood peace and protection, something the Broken had never truly known, and in return the Murkblood helped Toranaku rouse the creatures of the mine, at great cost, hoping to make it unlivable and drive the Dragonmaw off the island. Their overseer told the secret only to the one he knew to be the Netherwing's ally.

title: Kurdran Wildhammer
body: Kurdran Wildhammer is the thane of the Wildhammer dwarves in Outland. In the Second War he fought the Horde on the back of his gryphon, Sky'ree, and was credited with slaying nine dragons. When the Alliance expedition crossed the Dark Portal he led its gryphon riders, and when Ner'zhul's portals began to tear Draenor apart he chose to stay behind with his comrades so that the Portal could be sealed. Azeroth mourned him as dead for twenty years. He and Sky'ree survived, and now he holds Wildhammer Stronghold against the Legion's siege, receiving visitors inside while his keeper tends the faithful gryphon who would die for him.

title: Overlord Or'barokh
body: Overlord Or'barokh commands Shadowmoon Village for the Horde, with the elite Kor'kron guard at his back. Caught between the Legion's infernals and Illidan's armies, he has no men to spare and says so bluntly: when a shaman came pleading for soldiers, he asked whether the shaman had no eyes for the demons at the door and advised a prayer to the gods instead, for the Horde could not help. What he does have are recruits, and every newcomer is a grunt to him. His wind riders bring him word of the valley, lately of Eclipsion armies mustering on the Path of Conquest.

parts.body: It was Or'barokh's plan that broke the Eclipsion advance. A concoction brewed by Researcher Tiorus, poured over a stolen tabard, let a grunt pass as one of Illidan's elves and strike the colossi of the Eclipsion Fields, and the giants of Shadowmoon turned against the elves who had courted them.

title: Earthmender Torlok
body: Earthmender Torlok of the Earthen Ring keeps vigil at the Altar of Damnation, trying to make amends to the elements of Shadowmoon. He is an orc, and he does not hide that it was his own people who wounded them: here, he says, Gul'dan severed the tie between the orcs and the spirits, and not content with the ruin of the draenei, razed Draenor itself for power. The spirits he finds are enraged and unwilling to speak, so he gathers their souls in a totem until they can be heard.

parts.body: When at last the spirits answered, they named Cyrukh the Firelord, an elemental lord unearthed by Gul'dan's ritual, and Torlok cursed the warlock for a damned fool. Without the words to call the firelord forth, and with no idea where to seek them, he sent for an old hermit he had once met.

title: Oronok Torn-heart
body: Oronok Torn-heart lives as a hermit farmer on the Shattered Shelf above Coilskar Cistern, where his trained felboars dig tubers from the hard earth of the plains below. He invites travelers to sit by his fire, and admits that he has been a lot of things, though what he once was matters less to him than what he is now: a farmer. Flayers from a nest to the northeast prey on his animals, and he shows them no mercy. To strangers who come asking after words of damnation he says he has never heard of them, and advises them to let the dead rest.

parts.body: Oronok was once a lieutenant of Gul'dan, a shaman who had abandoned the elements for shadow magic, and he stood beside the warlock at the Altar of Damnation when the land was shattered. Like every orc on Draenor he felt the cut. Sick at heart, he gathered his boys and fled to the hills, and it has taken him twenty years to reach the elements again. When he learned what Illidan had done with Gul'dan's words, he sent his three sons, Grom'tor the warrior, Ar'tor the hunter and Borak the scholar, to recover them.

Not every son came home. Ar'tor's spirit sent back his bow and the second piece of the cipher with a last message: that he died free, that the hunting grounds are glorious, and that he waits there for his father. Oronok shed a single tear, then promised that a song of honor would be written for the one who brought the news.

title: Akama
body: Akama leads the Ashtongue, the most feared tribe of the Broken, whose most vicious warriors he picks by hand. At Illidan's command his people dig in the Ruins of Baa'ri under his lieutenant Oronu, who receives written orders from him daily, and his Ashtongue Deathsworn hold the Warden's Cage, a prison rumored to be a torture chamber. To the Aldor and the Scryers he is evil and cunning, and the draenei mourn what became of one once so wise and beloved. To many of his own people he is a traitor and Illidan's lapdog, and Akama says it is best that they go on thinking so, for now.

parts.body: Akama serves Illidan only in appearance. He joined the Betrayer because visions foretold that his race would otherwise be destroyed, and he has waited ever since for further signs: Velen's exodus, the opening of the Dark Portal, the coming of heroes from Azeroth. The brutes at Baa'ri were chosen to keep up the mask he shows Illidan, only his Deathsworn know his true mind, and in a hidden chamber of the Warden's Cage he guards Maiev Shadowsong and bides his time.

With it, he said, he and his Deathsworn could destroy Illidan and rule Outland in his place. But that was not the vision he had been granted, nor how his people would be freed, and he asked that the crystal be taken to A'dal.

title: Maiev Shadowsong
body: Maiev Shadowsong is the Warden who held Illidan captive for ten thousand years and hunted him all the way to Outland after he escaped. Now she is the prisoner, locked in a cell in the Warden's Cage under the watch of Akama and his Deathsworn. Akama insists that they want the same thing and that she must wait, for he has spent years preparing and cannot tip his hand too soon. Maiev will have none of it. She is no pawn in his game, she tells him, and when she unleashes her wrath on Illidan it will have nothing to do with his foolish scheme. If Illidan is to die, it will be by her hand.

title: Neltharaku
body: Neltharaku is the patron of the Netherwing, a nether dragon who flies high above the Netherwing Fields, where his young dare not land for fear of the Dragonmaw. He is a father in grief. The orcs have taken many of his children to Dragonmaw Fortress and tortured them until they gave in, and his mate Karynaku is chained atop its walls; every attempt he has made to free her has failed. Neltharaku feels powerless against them. It was Illidan, he says, who found the Dragonmaw their leader, Zuluhed, the orc held responsible for the capture of the Dragon Aspect Alexstrasza. If such an orc could take an Aspect, how could the young Netherwing resist him?

parts.body: Neltharaku found a way to fight back after all. Nethervine crystals charged with his own essence broke the riders' hold over his enslaved children and turned them on their captors, and at last Zuluhed the Whacked was slain and Karynaku freed from her chains atop the fortress.

title: Overlord Mor'ghor
body: Overlord Mor'ghor rules the Dragonmaw Base Camp on Netherwing Ledge, a coarse and boastful fel orc who serves Illidan and drives his workers to strip the island bare. He was once a chief lieutenant of the Dragonmaw at Grim Batol on Azeroth, a past the black dragonflight has not forgotten. Recruits who arrive with service papers start as peons, and the few who survive rise in rank under his eye. He sends his captains against the Legion on the Twilight Ridge and his commanders against the Aldor and the Scryers. He also keeps dealings of his own: the Netherwing eggs his orcs collect are sought by Lady Sinestra, who speaks for a black dragon master Mor'ghor had believed dead.

parts.body: Mor'ghor's pride betrayed him. He named his finest orc the first highlord of the Dragonmaw, and Illidan himself came to the ledge to see this hero. The master saw through the disguise at once, called Mor'ghor an incompetent buffoon who had been deceived, and declared the whole operation compromised. Mor'ghor was ordered to deliver the impostor's carcass within the hour.

title: Illidari Lord Balthas
body: Illidari Lord Balthas is an eredar in Illidan's service who stands among the Dragonmaw at their base camp on Netherwing Ledge. His brother, Reth'hedron the Subduer, chose the other side and now lords over the Twilight Ridge in Nagrand for the Burning Legion. With the Sha'tar bringing war to the gates of the Black Temple, Balthas admits that the Illidari cannot spare the strength to slay an eredar of such power. He has a better plan: to subdue Reth'hedron and banish him back through the Twilight Portal with a soul cannon built for the task.

parts.body: The soul cannon was attuned to Balthas's own blood, the same blood that flows in Reth'hedron's veins, and fired from the air it drove the Subduer from the ridge. Balthas warns that his brother will be back, but for now the Legion's war against Illidan is weakened.

title: Doomwalker
body: Doomwalker is a fel reaver unlike any other, a towering war engine of the Burning Legion, mightier than the lesser reavers that roam Outland. It prowls the approaches west of the Black Temple, between the Ruins of Karabor and the Ata'mal Terrace, and greets intruders in a cold, mechanical voice, warning them to proceed no farther or be eliminated. When it strikes, it speaks of tectonic disruption and the ground trembles, and over each fallen foe it pronounces the same verdict: threat level zero, directive accomplished.

title: The Legion's Bombardment
body: Infernals fall on Wildhammer Stronghold and Shadowmoon Village day and night, flung from Legion Hold, and the defenders of both outposts are close to breaking. Wing Commander Nuainn's riders are ragged and exhausted, and Blood Guard Gulmok drafts every able fighter onto the line, for even the Kor'kron cannot hold forever. Holding out is not enough. The hold is nigh impregnable and neither outpost can spare the forces for an assault, so each sends a volunteer into Legion Hold in disguise, to overhear the Legion's commanders and learn their plans.

parts.body: The news from the hold is grim. Listening at its communication device, the spies heard an image of Warbringer Razuun, speaking for Doom Lord Kazzak, order the attacks stepped up to destroy the orcish and dwarven strongholds, and promise infernals enough from the Deathforge to do it.

Scouts at Deathforge Tower and Slag Watch then guided the assault on the forge itself, where the summoning ritual was broken and Razuun was slain. His orders pointed to the true staging ground, Invasion Point: Cataclysm, high in the mountains and reached only by a teleporter in Legion Hold.

title: The Cipher of Damnation
body: Shadowmoon's elements are in torment. Here Gul'dan's ritual severed the orcs from the spirits of Draenor, and the spirits of the valley remain so tortured that they refuse to commune with the Earthen Ring. At the Altar of Damnation, on the western outskirts of the Hand of Gul'dan, Earthmender Torlok sets out to make amends. With a totem of spirits he gathers the souls of enraged fire and earth, then of water from the naga's fouled pools at Coilskar, then of air from the crystal fields of the Netherwing, until the spirits of every element can be heard together.

parts.body: When the spirits finally spoke, they named Cyrukh the Firelord, an elemental lord unearthed by Gul'dan's ritual. Only the ritual's own words could call him forth to be destroyed, and with no idea where to find them, Torlok sent for an old hermit he had once met, Oronok Torn-heart.
sources: creature_text 21024
quest 10513 description

parts.body: The hermit was no farmer. Oronok confessed that he had stood beside Gul'dan as his lieutenant when the land was shattered. The words have a name, the Cipher of Damnation: kept for twenty years in Gul'dan's quarters inside Karabor, they were found by Illidan when he took the Black Temple and split among his servants. Oronok's three sons have gone after the pieces.
sources: quest 10519

parts.body: Grom'tor, the eldest, a warrior with his mother's temper, beat the hiding place of one piece out of a Coilskar naga commander. It lay in a naga chest at Coilskar, and the first fragment of the cipher went home to his father in a lockbox.

Ar'tor, the youngest, was found dead at Illidari Point, held in the air by demonic crystals. Freed, his spirit would not rest until his task was done: he won back his family bow, Lohn'goron, and with it took the second fragment from Veneratus the Many before he passed on to the hunting grounds.

Borak, the scholar turned silent assassin, baited Illidan's envoy with bloodthistle to part him from his bodyguard, then sent an agent disguised as one of the elves into Eclipse Point with false orders for Grand Commander Ruusk. The fragment was set on the move toward Zuluhed, and Borak ambushed its bearer, Ruul the Darkener, to take the third.

Made whole and read aloud at the Altar of Damnation, where the memory of Gul'dan stands, the cipher called up the memories imprinted on the land, and then Cyrukh himself. The firelord was destroyed, and the elements had what they asked for.

title: The Return of Teron Gorefiend
body: The ghosts of Shadowmoon have grown restless. At Wildhammer Stronghold, Zorus the Judicator warns that the dwarves built upon the ancestral grounds of the Shadowmoon orcs, whose spirits lay dormant for nearly twenty years until something stirred them. At Shadowmoon Village, Chief Apothecary Hildagard says the whole land is haunted. Each crafts goggles from the ever-burning ash of the fel lava pools, letting their wearer see the dead, and sends the wearer to destroy the spirits that wander the outpost.

parts.body: The spirits cleared from the outposts whispered one name: Teron Gorefiend. He was a warlock of Gul'dan, and when he was slain, Gul'dan placed his soul inside the body of a slain knight of Stormwind, making the first death knight of the Horde. He has long been thought dead, and even the Forsaken tremble at his legend.

parts.body: The trail led to an ancient Shadowmoon spirit at the Altar of Shadows, beyond the Netherwing Fields. After the Second War, the spirit said, Gorefiend returned to Draenor with his death knights and, unable to bear what he had become, took his own life. If Gorefiend walks again, the spirit offered to divine it, once his armor, cloak and truncheon were found.

parts.body: With the relics restored, the spirit dropped its mask. The tale had been a lie: the Altar of Shadows was a prison, and the spirit was Teron Gorefiend himself. He seized his helper's body to strike down his jailers, beginning with Karsius the Ancient Watcher.

title: The Medallion of Karabor
body: The Aldor at the Altar of Sha'tar and the Scryers at the Sanctum of the Stars both learn that the Ashtongue are digging in the Ruins of Baa'ri on Illidan's orders, and both send agents to seize the Tablets of Baa'ri before the Broken can. Baa'ri was buried with its people and its holy relics when Gul'dan raised the volcano, and the tablets are rumored to hold the secrets of the Temple of Karabor, the place now known as the Black Temple. Whatever they reveal could aid the fight against Illidan.

parts.body: The tablets spoke of a Medallion of Karabor kept at Baa'ri. Only the highest-ranking draenei priests were granted such medallions, for they opened the way into the Temple of Karabor. Orders in Akama's own hand, carried to his lieutenant Oronu the Elder, would show whether the Ashtongue had found it.
sources: quests 10571, 10684 descriptions

parts.body: Akama's orders revealed that four fragments of the medallion had been unearthed and given to the Ashtongue Corruptors, Broken shaman who now defile the elements. Won from them, the four make only half the medallion. Akama must hold the rest, and the trail leads to his prison, the Warden's Cage.
sources: quests 10574, 10575, 10685, 10686 descriptions

parts.body: At the cage Akama's second, Sanoru, was waiting: Akama has followed the visitor's progress closely. The Ashtongue slain at Baa'ri, Sanoru admits, were brutes hand-picked to keep up a facade for Illidan, and only the Deathsworn know Akama's true intentions. First, the visitor must prove they are not with Illidan by slaying Zandras, the satyr who spies on the prison for him.

parts.body: Through a passage hidden by stagnant water, Akama waited in a secret chamber. He confessed that he serves Illidan only in appearance, bound to him by visions that foretold his race's destruction otherwise, and that he has waited years for the signs to come to pass, the latest of them the arrival of heroes from Azeroth.
sources: quest 10628 description and reward text

parts.body: The fragments were replicas. Akama holds the true Medallion of Karabor, kept secret from Illidan, but it lacks a final piece. The Ashtongue seer Udalo, held in the Arcatraz, sent word in dreams that he had found it, and died there before he could say more, leaving one word scrawled beneath him: Ata'mal.

Taken from Shadowlord Deathwail, it carried the power Akama had once seen Velen wield, and he was tempted to keep it. Instead he asked that it be taken somewhere safe, to A'dal in Shattrath.

title: Illidan's Pupil
body: Aldor and Scryer scouts alike report a massive influx of Sunfury blood elf recruits heading to the Ruins of Karabor, before the walls of the Black Temple. In itself that would be a plain military threat, but the scouts describe the recruits' attire and fighting style as suspiciously close to Illidan's own. Exarch Onaala of the Aldor and Larissa Sunstrike of the Scryers will not raise the alarm without good reason, so each sends an agent into the ruins to bring back the recruits' weapons and settle whether the fear is founded.

parts.body: The glaives taken from the initiates are authentic. Illidan is training blood elf demon hunters at Karabor, whose power will be turned on the Aldor and the Scryers as often as on any demon. To buy time, Onaala and Larissa mean to loose upon his captors the pit lord Azaloth, kept banished because he proved too strong for the lessons.

quests 10637, 10688 descriptions

parts.body: With Azaloth loose, the orders sent their agents to western Nagrand after a rumor: a demon hunter named Altruis, one of the rare few of his kind who owe Illidan no allegiance, is said to live out there. He might be willing to explain what is being taught at Karabor.
sources: quests 10640, 10689 descriptions (Nagrand-filed, left to Shadowmoon)

parts.body: Once convinced, Altruis told the tale of Varedis. Of five warriors Kael'thas sent to train under Illidan, three died and one went mad; Varedis alone survived and within a year surpassed the three masters set to teach him. He had stolen into the Shadow Council and learned by heart the Book of Fel Names, said to hold the true name of every demon, and now he runs Karabor at Illidan's request.
sources: npc_text 10492-10495 (Altruis's tale)

parts.body: The book itself was taken from the Shadow Labyrinth. Altruis, tempted by its power, sent it back with a warning: burn it in Varedis's presence once he takes his demon form. At Karabor the book was burned before him, stripping his power, and Varedis fell with Alandien, Theras and Netharel.

title: The Plight of the Netherwing
body: Over the Netherwing Fields the nether drakes are starving. Something has them so frightened that they will not come down even to feed, and some fall from the sky, dead from exhaustion before they reach the ground. Mordenai, who watches over them, begs for help: kill the Rocknail flayers among the crystals, the drakes' natural prey, and lay the carcasses out in the field, then stand very still, for a drake will come down to eat as long as no one makes an aggressive move.

parts.body: That kindness reached the flight's patron, Neltharaku, who soars high above. He told of Dragonmaw Fortress, where the Dragonmaw torture captured drakes into obedience; of Zuluhed, the orc Illidan gave them as leader, who once captured the Aspect Alexstrasza; and of his own mate Karynaku, chained atop the fortress after every attempt to free her had failed.
sources: npc_text 10614, 10615, 10616 (Neltharaku's tale, quest 10814)

parts.body: To buy him time, the orcs in the fortress were cut down while Neltharaku devised a remedy. From nethervine crystals gathered on Netherwing Ledge he made charms filled with his own essence, which break the riders' hold over their enslaved drakes and set them free to turn on their captors.

Then came the climb to the top of the fortress. Karynaku, weakened by her chains, called Zuluhed the Whacked to her with a false promise to obey, and when the old chieftain appeared he was slain for his key. She was free at last.
sources: creature_text 11980 (Zuluhed)

parts.body: Karynaku carried her rescuer back to Mordenai, who rejoiced that his mother was free and his brothers and sisters saved. He named the stranger kin to the Netherwing Dragonflight, to be welcomed with open arms whenever the flight calls again.

title: Among the Dragonmaw
body: Sworn by blood oath to help the Netherwing retake their lands and see their bloodline born anew, an ally is sent into the heart of the enemy. Netherwing Ledge, once the flight's sanctuary, is now home to the Dragonmaw, but the flight's magic there is still strong enough to cloak a stranger as a fel orc of Illidan Stormrage. Carrying service papers prepared by the Netherwing, the newcomer flies to Dragonmaw Base Camp to present them to Overlord Mor'ghor and begin a new life in the ranks of the clan.

parts.body: Mor'ghor laughed at the papers and made the newcomer a peon. Daily labor for Taskmaster Varkule covers the true work, done for Yarzill the Merc, whose eyes flicker blue when no one is watching: he is a Netherwing agent in disguise. Under his direction the peon poisons peon camps, ambushes transporters on the Dragonmaw Skyway and hunts the stolen Netherwing eggs.

parts.body: The infiltrator rose through the ranks, from peon to overseer, from overseer to captain, and at last to commander, a promotion Illidan himself asked for, making the newcomer the first Dragonmaw ever to hold that rank outside the Black Temple.

parts.body: Ordered to sack the Scryer or the Aldor outpost, the commander warned them instead. Their defenders sprang a trap on the Dragonmaw raiders, and Mor'ghor, shown medals as proof of victory, laughed with delight and ordered such a raid every day.

parts.body: At last Mor'ghor named his finest orc the first highlord of the Dragonmaw, and Illidan himself came to the ledge to see this hero. He saw through the disguise at once and declared the whole operation compromised. Yarzill snatched the highlord to safety on his back, and word of what came next waits with Barthamus in Shattrath's Lower City.

title: The Dark Conclave
body: The ghosts of the Sketh'lon arakkoa are stirring in their ruined camp northwest of the Deathforge. Gryphonrider Kieran's scouts report that the spirits wield powers no one knew they had and seem to be organizing, and at Shadowmoon Village Sergeant Kargrul hears that they prey on the peons sent to cut wood among the ruins, draining their lives to fuel their magic. Both send agents into the Sketh'lon Wreckage to take whatever writings the ghosts carry and learn what drives the Dark Conclave.

parts.body: The journal pages taken from the ghosts are mostly unintelligible, but they speak of an elaborate ritual prepared up to the moment the arakkoa died, of a spell gone awry, and of a deserter. The best lead is to find him: a haunted arakkoa named Parshah, waiting by the road through the Magma Fields.
sources: quests 10569, 10760 reward texts

parts.body: Parshah is the deserter. He tells how his people, seeing the Horde mass under Gul'dan, prepared to strike him first, and how the warlock answered with a spell that destroyed their camps and twisted their spirits. The Dark Conclave must be stopped before it unleashes a greater evil, and he means to build a staff to do it, beginning with the war totem carried by Asghar.
sources: quests 10759, 10761 reward texts
quest 10777 description

parts.body: Gul'dan's magic fed on the spell the arakkoa were preparing and forged a sinister force that engulfed their spirits. Parshah built his staff from Asghar's totem, the Rod of Lianthe taken from Eclipse Point and Sketh'lon feathers, its headpiece charged with the echoes of Gul'dan at the Altar of Damnation. The ghosts mean to summon an ancient evil in the lava pits south of their base camp.
sources: quest 10808 description

parts.body: With the staff the ritual was broken, and the Dark Conclave threatens no more. Parshah had sought a way to stop them for years and often felt guilty for abandoning his kin; now he knows he made the right choice, for without his wavering conscience he might have become a shade among them.

title: The Illidari-Bane Blade
body: Shards of a strange metal turn up among the mo'arg of Legion Hold, who seem to be working with fragments of it everywhere. The pieces look like parts of a larger weapon, sharp and etched with runes that glow with a menacing light, and their purpose is far from clear. Whoever finds one soon carries it to a weaponsmith of the outposts, Ordinn Thunderfist at Wildhammer Stronghold or Grokom Deatheye at Shadowmoon Village, for only a smith's eye can say what the Legion is making.

parts.body: Both smiths know the work. The metal is a rare ore enchanted to destroy demons, a secret weapon the Legion means to turn against Illidan's forces. The two pit lords of Legion Hold, Makazradon and Morgroron, already bear glaives made from it, and with their weapons captured there would be metal enough for a blade.
sources: quests 10621, 10623 reward texts
quests 10626, 10627 descriptions

parts.body: Forging the metal proved beyond both smiths. They sent the ingots to David Wayne, a blacksmith who came to Draenor with the Sons of Lothar and later left the expedition to live alone in Terokkar Forest; even Grokom admitted it pained him to send Horde business to a human. Wayne agreed to try, though most of the magic was gone, and warned that he would need some exotic resources.
sources: quests 10662, 10663 descriptions and reward texts

parts.body: Wayne needed rare things: an overcharged manacell from the Mechanar, the Lexicon Demonica from the Shadow Labyrinth, underworld loam from the Steamvault and the Tear of the Earthmother from the Shattered Halls. With them he forged the sword, and it was quenched in the Scalding Pools of the Hand of Gul'dan, a blade to cut down Illidari and Legion demons alike.
